name: obsidian-brain
tagline: A plugin that stores session capture and curated knowledge in an Obsidian vault. Shared runtime logic serves Claude and Codex; installed client certification requires separate native evidence.

language.name: Python
language.notes: stdlib only — no pip dependencies; deterministic hooks safe to run at session boundaries

framework.name: Claude Code and Codex plugin packages

ui.notes: dashboards only — the plugin itself requires no Obsidian plugin to write notes

realtime.endpoint: direct filesystem writes — no MCP server, no REST API, no daemon

ai.provider: Invoking native Claude or Codex CLI through ai_backend.execute_ai
ai.model: Selected native configuration or an explicit provider model setting; observed model provenance is retained
ai.notes: Bounded read-only analysis jobs run from skills, not capture hooks. No other-host fallback. Codex automatic capture remains off until current frontend binding is proven.

vectorSearch.engine: SQLite FTS5 (BM25) + 7-signal rerank; TF-IDF cosine themes with ACT-R activation and Free-Energy surprise

diagram.intro: Claude and Codex descriptors enter the selected-host runtime. Capture retains known facts, private unresolved references and immutable checkpoints before revision-checked publication. Native AI uses the invoking host. Installed Codex current-client binding remains unavailable; automatic Codex capture skips without retaining a source. Source tests do not certify native client acceptance.

nodes.label: Shared Runtime + Transactions
nodes.sub: context · scrub · source revisions · capture checkpoints

tiers.arrowLabel: OS ownership + prepared journal → atomic note → cursor

notes: Claude and Codex lifecycle descriptors are implemented. Actual installed-client dispatch and full parity acceptance remain pending.
Vault OS ownership precedes session ownership. A living holder is never stolen by age; process death releases OS ownership.
Atomic note publication follows a durable prepared operation. Cursor acknowledgment follows verified applied publication.
Managed capture/summary hashes protect manual edits. Deferred AI receives an exact pre-generation source revision and runs without vault ownership.
Search-index rebuilds leave the durable coordination database intact. Classification caches use separate private OS ownership and semantic provenance.

capture_revision is SHA256 of the normalized managed capture region. applied_revision hashes the whole published note. summary_revision will identify the capture revision summarized; it is not a full-note hash.
Native lifecycle fixture subprocesses exercise the shared handlers. They do not prove desktop conversation hook dispatch or shipped Codex parity.

layers.name: Lifecycle Hooks (auto-running Python)
layers.description: Both plugin descriptors select native_entry.py through their host-specific hooks manifest. Verified contexts dispatch bounded capture/recovery without AI. Missing current-client identity skips capture and retains no source. Legacy facades remain explicit compatibility paths.

components.name: obsidian_session_log.py
components.purpose: Compatibility SessionEnd facade. Bound native contexts delegate to the shared lifecycle dispatcher; only explicit unbound Claude compatibility uses the legacy raw-session path. Installed hook manifests invoke native_entry.py directly.

components.name: obsidian_session_hint.py
components.purpose: Compatibility SessionStart facade. Bound native contexts delegate to shared startup and bounded registered-source recovery. Explicit unbound Claude compatibility retains its bootstrap and legacy context hint. Installed hooks use native_entry.py.

components.name: obsidian_context_snapshot.py
components.purpose: Compatibility PreCompact facade. Bound contexts delegate to shared native capture and immutable checkpoint snapshots. Explicit unbound Claude compatibility retains legacy snapshot controls. Installed hooks use native_entry.py.

components.name: obsidian_session_reaper.py
components.purpose: Bound contexts recover registered sources with source/time bounds and native origin identity. The explicit unbound Claude compatibility path retains its watermark-based orphan scan. These paths do not invent publication counts.

components.name: obsidian_retro_gate.py
components.purpose: Compatibility Stop facade. Bound contexts use the selected native lifecycle decision and session-scoped classification state; explicit unbound Claude compatibility retains its legacy sentinel behavior. Installed hooks use native_entry.py.

components.name: hooks.json
components.purpose: Claude hooks/hooks.json and Codex hooks/codex-hooks.json select native_entry.py for SessionStart, Stop, PreCompact and SessionEnd. Claude binds claude-code explicitly. Codex passes the pre-launch declaration and requires verified CLI ancestry with --no-daemon; shared-server, Desktop, missing or conflicting identity skips before runtime access. Native delivery still requires acceptance evidence.

layers.name: Shared Core (obsidian_utils)
layers.description: Explicit host context, bounded native transcripts, retained capture facts, secret scrubbing, native AI and revision-checked vault publication. Installed-client acceptance remains pending.

components.name: RuntimeContext
components.purpose: Resolves explicitly selected host and client, canonical project root, frozen native home, config, vault, shared index and private host state. Codex requires codex-cli or codex-desktop; unresolved frontend identity returns a diagnostic instead of guessing. brain_cli routes bounded context, capture, recovery, hooks and trusted skill operations.

components.name: load_config()
components.purpose: Bound RuntimeContext configuration is authoritative and frozen. Explicit unbound compatibility reads machine-local JSON over deepcopy(_DEFAULTS). Side-effect: auto-chmods the config to 0600 if group/world bits are set. indexed_folders(config) (#383) returns the folders user-facing search indexes, [sessions_folder, insights_folder, wiki_folder] (wiki_folder default claude-wiki; empty disables it; an invalid value is dropped with a warning). Every skill and top-level scripts/ ensure_index/rebuild_index call uses it (scripts/dev-test/ exempt); tests/test_indexed_folders.py parses each call's folder argument and fails unless it is the helper call, with a per-call allow-list for build_context_brief and open_item_dedup, which receive folders as parameters. _sync deletes only under scanned folders, so wiki rows survive those calls, except when ensure_index recreates a corrupt or legacy DB from the folders it was given. strict=True (used by /vault-reindex and /obsidian-setup, whose rebuild prunes rows outside its folders) raises on an invalid wiki_folder instead of dropping it. load_config(fresh=True) skips the per-session config cache.

components.name: get_session_context() / SID resolution
components.purpose: Single source of truth for session id, 4-char hash, project, and session-note name. Layer 0 is the harness's own CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, validated by FORMAT only and trusted ahead of every scan layer (#330): layers 1-4 all resolve by newest-mtime over a project directory, which cannot tell two concurrently-live sessions in one repo apart, so each could get the other's id. It was also unstable rather than merely wrong - a real vault note carried source_session hashing to f157 while its backlink named df46, because two calls inside one note write resolved via different winners, and get_session_context()'s cache cannot pin that since the cache key IS the resolved sid. The env value is constant for the session, so repeated calls agree, and it short-circuits the glob - measured on one machine, order of magnitude only: ~9.7us for the env read vs ~15.9ms for a glob over the 2259 transcripts in this project's own directory. Not gated on transcript existence - a new session has no JSONL yet and falling through in that window is the bug itself; a one-time WARN reports a well-formed id with no transcript. allow_env=False keeps check_hook_status() validating against the JSONLs rather than the env var. Where the env var is absent, resolution falls back to newest-mtime over the project directory - the same heuristic used before #330. A stricter concurrency-ambiguity refusal (refuse rather than guess when 2+ transcripts were touched within a measured window of each other) was built and then REMOVED before release: measured correctly - per transcript, was another transcript in the same project dir touched within the window at-or-before its own last write - it would have refused 69.2% of 3892 real transcripts, because agent/teammate fan-out writes its own top-level <sid>.jsonl into the same project directory and those files are indistinguishable from a second real session by anything this resolver can see. Layer 0 already closes the original #330 bug wherever the env var is available; see docs/plans/330-session-id-crossing.md's 'Reversed after adversarial review' note. The bootstrap fast path's same-second mtime tie-break (trust the cached sid when its JSONL ties the newest) is the original, pre-#330 behaviour. Single source of truth for session id, 4-char hash, project, and session-note name. Layered SID chain: project-basename to bootstrap fast-path to slow JSONL glob (newest mtime) to unknown; the cross-project recent-bootstrap scan is reachable ONLY when cwd yields no basename at all (the deleted-worktree case) so a readable cwd can never inherit another repo's session. The suffix glob over ~/.claude/projects/*<project>/ unions every encoding CC may have written (both '_' and '.' fold to '-') and is filtered to the directories belonging to the current cwd — arbitrated against the authoritative cwd field inside the transcripts themselves whenever the encoding guess is ambiguous or suspect, with that guess acting as pre-filter only — refusing rather than guessing when none is ours. The bootstrap fast path derives its cached-sid view by filtering that single restricted glob, so a refusal can never be read as 'no other transcripts exist'. Layer 0's own existence probe globs a NARROWED suffix (one specific sid's filename) directly, WITHOUT going through that restriction/arbitration step, so it can never memoize a 'cannot tell' verdict under the same cache key the later, broad glob would hit (#354 review item 4 - the narrow probe and the broad glob inspect different files but would otherwise collide on the same _dirs_by_transcript_cwd memo key). The layer-4 gate keys on the SOURCE of the basename (cwd vs CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR), keeping the #105 deleted-worktree recovery reachable. WARNs on this path are one-shot per distinct cause (guarded by a lock against concurrent upgrade_batch() worker threads double-printing the same warning), since it re-runs once per note inside read_note_metadata(). Cached contexts are keyed by sid alone, so each carries the cwd it was resolved from and is discarded with a stderr WARN when that no longer matches. SID filenames validated against a safe charset to block path traversal.

components.name: canonical_project_name()
components.purpose: Resolves the main-repo basename via the git common-dir so all worktrees of a repo collapse under one logical project; normalizes spaces/underscores to hyphens; one-shot stderr warning only on genuine git failure.

components.name: read_transcript() / extract_*_messages()
components.purpose: Parses CC JSONL transcripts (nested message.content and flat shapes), extracting user/assistant messages and tool uses.

components.name: extract_session_metadata()
components.purpose: Derives project, project_path, git_branch, files_touched (<=60), errors (<=30), duration_minutes, and commits from a transcript.

components.name: generate_summary() / generate_snapshot_summary()
components.purpose: Bound native summary/theme helpers call the shared AI backend with inline scrubbed input and the selected host context. Parallel workers receive that context explicitly. Summary publication binds the result to retained capture/source revisions and managed summary regions; manual prose survives and later capture remains queued when a stale result conflicts. Legacy unbound compatibility cannot silently select a native provider.

components.name: write_vault_note()
components.purpose: Legacy-compatible writer wrapper around NoteMutation/apply_mutations. Validates containment before side effects and accepts an optional expected_revision captured before generation. Returns None only for applied/unchanged publication; conflict/pending results remain errors. New notes use 0600. Atomic publication and operation recovery belong to note_transactions.py.

components.name: resolve_source_session_note()
components.purpose: Returns the source_session_note wikilink stem only when the target note EXISTS and its own frontmatter session_id equals the source_session being stamped beside it; returns "" otherwise so callers omit the field rather than write a contradicting backlink (#330 AC-3). Path-contained with resolve()/is_relative_to() like write_vault_note(), because session_note_name is composed by make_filename() over a slugified cwd basename - not free-form input, but not a literal either, and a traversing value would read frontmatter from an arbitrary file and vouch for it as a session note. ADVISORY, not enforced: note frontmatter is assembled by SKILL.md prose (note_writer.py is content-blind and never composes these fields), so decide/error-log/compress/retro each call this helper by instruction and nothing prevents a future caller composing the field blind. Deliberately NOT used by obsidian_context_snapshot.py, whose source_session_note is a forward reference to a parent note SessionEnd has not written yet and which vault_index.py parses to pair snapshots with parents; a regression test pins that.

components.name: scrub_secrets() / escape_wikilinks()
components.purpose: Best-effort redaction of GitHub/AWS tokens, password/secret/api_key assignments, PEM headers and Bearer values before any user content reaches the vault; escapes double-brackets so bash test brackets do not create phantom Obsidian links.

components.name: claim_hook_run() / release_hook_run()
components.purpose: Explicit legacy dedup helpers retain their compatibility behavior. Native capture uses durable operation identity and vault/session OS ownership; contention retains pending facts without publishing unowned writes.

components.name: gather_session_evidence()
components.purpose: For /retro: collects all snapshots (matched on frontmatter session_id) plus insights/decisions/error-fixes/retros (matched on frontmatter source_session) whose id matches the active session id OR any id in the keyword-only also_session_ids (#184 — recovers evidence written under a prior session id across a compact boundary), with discovery_errors captured rather than raised. session_id and also_session_ids are normalized into the ordered, de-duplicated bundle['session_ids'] (dropping '', 'unknown', and duplicates); snapshots are deduped by stem across ids and each snapshot/insight/decision/error-fix/retro entry carries its own session_id so callers can label pre-compact-arc evidence. bundle['retros'] (#285) holds prior claude-retro notes matched the same source_session way as insights — a boundary marker for /retro's Step 3a scoping, not evidence to mine itself. A parse failure is recorded only when it means the note is BROKEN: the missing-opening-fence verdict (frontmatter.NO_OPENING_FENCE_REASON, matched exactly on the raw reason so the filter cannot fail open when vault_index's classifier is unavailable) means 'this file is not a note' — a dashboard, export or scratch .md in the insights folder — and is filtered, because this parse runs before the source_session filter and one such file would otherwise raise /retro's 'evidence discovery partially or fully failed' banner in every project, every session, permanently; no_closing_fence / frontmatter_too_long / unreadable are kept. Every reason that does get recorded is rendered through _describe_note_parse_failure() first, which collapses the split_frontmatter verdicts to a closed-set category (deliberate conservatism: only the shape-stop variant actually embeds up to 60 characters of the note's own text, but all three are categorized together) while passing the content-free 'unreadable file: <strerror>' shape through intact.

components.name: recurring_themes_section()
components.purpose: For /recall: renders a '## Recurring Themes' markdown block listing the project's top themes by activation (via themes.get_top_themes_for_project), each with a name, a one-line summary lead, and (N notes). Fails open to '' on any error or when no themes exist (#231).

components.name: build_context_brief()
components.purpose: Builds the /recall context brief entirely in Python (no sub-agent): reads session/insight files directly, composes the brief + load-manifest, appends each session's indented snapshot rows via fetch_snapshot_summaries() — which since #70 discovers DATE-AGNOSTICALLY (the `date` argument is retained for the four-positional-arg calls in skills/vault-search and skills/vault-ask but no longer filters) so a PreCompact snapshot written before midnight is still found under the next day's session note, and reads it from find_snapshots_for_session(use_index=True), a process-lifetime memo of session_id → snapshot stems keyed by resolved sessions folder and invalidated on that folder's mtime, so an M-row history table costs ONE frontmatter scan instead of M; the memo is opt-in precisely so the SessionEnd write path, which creates a snapshot and then reads the list back, keeps the uncached scan, then runs open-item detection via open_item_dedup.collect_open_items(). Cross-references each open item's own source-session date against every OTHER scanned session's '## Summary' text: for every candidate session STRICTLY NEWER than the item's source (never same-date, never the item's own note), match_items_against_evidence() checks for a completion match; the highest-confidence strictly-newer hit is kept, tagged with contradicted_by (date) and contradicted_by_title, so /recall Step 4 renders a one-line 'looks done per session <date>' nudge instead of silently re-listing the item as still open (#264 Task 3, Fix B).

components.name: mark_/clear_/get_retro_classification_pending()
components.purpose: The retro-gate sentinel primitives backing the Stop hook: mark writes a session-scoped JSON sentinel under ~/.claude/obsidian-brain/retro-gate/ (sanitized sid, path-contained, atomic os.replace); get reads it (with created_at for TTL); clear removes it. /retro arms via mark after saving the note and disarms via clear once Step 7.5 classification is filed. mark refuses outright when the session id is empty, whitespace, or 'unknown', returning a "Failed:" string the skill echoes rather than writing a sentinel (#330): the Stop hook looks up the HARNESS id and would never find a gate filed under 'unknown', so arming there looks armed to the skill while enforcing nothing. Since #330 the arm side resolves via layer 0, the same id the harness puts in the Stop hook's stdin, so the two agree by construction.

components.name: _append_sessionend_log() / _append_reaper_log()
components.purpose: Writes one-line key=value outcome records to the hook telemetry log, rotating at 100 KB, 0600, sanitizing newlines/tabs. Primary diagnostic surface for sessions that did not produce a vault note.

components.name: hook_bootstrap.py
components.purpose: Import-failure fallback for the four lifecycle hooks (#371). Each hook wraps its top-level obsidian_utils import in try/except; on failure it calls log_import_failure(), which appends one outcome=IMPORT_FAILED line (python version + exception type/message) to the hook telemetry log with the same field order, 100 KB rotation and 0600 mode, then the hook exits 0. SessionStart also emits additionalContext telling the model the plugin did not load. Stdlib only, 3.9-safe, never imports obsidian_utils.

components.name: frontmatter.py — split_frontmatter() / split_lines_lf_crlf()
components.purpose: Stdlib-``re``-only module (#277) extracted from note_writer.py so note_writer.py, vault_index.py and obsidian_utils.py share exactly ONE bounded, shape-checked frontmatter splitter instead of independently-drifting copies. obsidian_utils.read_note_metadata() and _peek_frontmatter_field() joined as consumers in #283, retiring their own 40-line and 30-line bounds (which repeated the vault_index.py defect below — and neither of which had a real closing-fence guard: when no closing fence arrived within the bound, both harvested body prose into fields): both now read the frontmatter region up to its closing fence (capped at MAX_FRONTMATTER_LINES+1 lines / 2 MB for pathological files) and delegate the split. split_lines_lf_crlf() splits on '\r\n'/'\n' only (never a bare '\r', which can legitimately appear inside a pasted terminal redraw in a fenced code block). split_frontmatter() requires line 0 to be a bare '---', then scans for the closing '---' within MAX_FRONTMATTER_LINES (1000), requiring every intervening line to be blank, key:-shaped, a '- ' list item, or an indented continuation — a '# Title' heading or prose paragraph stops the scan and fails loudly instead of splicing frontmatter fields into the body. The 1000-line bound replaces an earlier independent 40-line bound in vault_index.py that silently dropped 28 real notes from the search index (closing fences as deep as line 460 in /emerge and /standup output with long projects: lists) — this module exists precisely so that kind of divergence can't happen again. Imports nothing from this package (obsidian_utils.py imports vault_index.py; note_writer.py imports obsidian_utils.py; vault_index.py importing note_writer.py directly would close that cycle, so all three import this leaf module instead).

components.name: note_writer.py
components.purpose: CLI backing deterministic vault note persistence for skills (#269): two subcommands, both reading note content from stdin (1 MB cap) and validating path safety before any filesystem side effect. write validates folder/filename (rejects absolute/home/'..'/dot-segment paths and non-bare-.md filenames, e.g. blocking a write into .obsidian/plugins/**) then delegates the write itself entirely to write_vault_note() for the shared revision-checked transaction boundary with 0600 notes. append-update (used by /compress's update-existing path) resolves and validates an EXISTING note path (containment + dot-segment reject + must-already-exist), then applies the update-text insertion (before the first trailing marker like '## Tool Usage'), an optional last_updated bump, and an optional tag merge (block- or flow-style tags:) in ONE atomic rewrite — never touching date/source_session/source_session_note/type, and preserving the note's own CRLF/LF line ending for every line it adds. Invoked via subprocess by 7 SKILL.md files (compress, decide, error-log, retro, standup, vault-import, vault-stats) instead of a Write tool call, so note persistence no longer depends on a context-blind helper sub-agent choosing to save. Both subcommands also validate the CONTENT they are handed, not just their arguments: empty/whitespace-only stdin, a note body without a '---' frontmatter fence pair, oversize stdin (rejected, never truncated), an empty or non-YYYY-MM-DD --last-updated, and a tag containing whitespace/':'/'#'/quotes (which would inject a frontmatter key or break tag indexing) are all ERROR + exit 1 with no filesystem side effect. write additionally refuses to replace an existing note unless --overwrite is passed (only /standup's in-place session-note upgrade passes it), restoring the collision loudness the Write tool used to provide. append-update owns the vault across its read/update and records the exact read revision. The shared vault ownership lock covers append publication; obsolete compatibility PID lock files cannot block it.

components.name: vault_scan.py
components.purpose: Read-only CLI for /vault-ask and /vault-search (#375, #312). grep lists the *.md files under one or more vault folders that match a regex. It matches one line at a time, like the ripgrep behind the Grep tool. It is the fallback when a session has no Grep tool. With --frontmatter-only it searches only the frontmatter block, which the Grep tool cannot do. Skills pass the pattern as --pattern=<regex>, so a pattern that starts with '-' is not read as a flag. Stdout is the sorted path list. On success (exit 0), stderr ends with 'vault_scan: N match(es), M file(s) scanned, K skipped (too_large=a, unreadable=b, outside_vault=c, bad_frontmatter=d, symlinked_dirs=e, unreadable_dirs=f)'. meta prints date, type, project, session_id, source_session_note, tags, title, snippet and error per file as JSON Lines. It parses the whole frontmatter with split_frontmatter(). The fixed Read(limit=40) it replaces dropped fields: frontmatter can run past line 40, and /emerge fences close as deep as line 461. It reuses note_writer's _validate_vault_path/_validate_folder. It checks every file with resolve() + is_relative_to() against the vault. It never descends a symlinked subfolder, and counts each one it skips. It skips files over 5 MB. It reports a parse failure as a content-free category. Exit 0 on success, 2 for bad arguments, 1 for an unexpected error or a missing dependency module; on 2 or 1 stderr has only an ERROR: line.

components.name: wiki.py — LLM wiki library + CLI
components.purpose: LLM wiki for /vault-ask answers (#383, #395, #396). JSON CLI: rule (the 80% ASD-STE100 writing rule), lookup (search_vault with note_type claude-wiki, reranked, logs access; top 3 as path/question/updated/rank), stale (per-source content-hash changed/missing, unverifiable when the page's fingerprint is missing or bad, its sources is not a list, or neither sources nor memory_sources is a non-empty list (a memory-only page is valid); block-style YAML lists and maps are read too; plus newer counting notes from a direct OR FTS query over the question's non-stopword terms, skipped when none remain), count (resolves cited names in the notes table; distinct notes by resolved file path; snapshots count as their parent; unresolved or ambiguous names returned as rejected; since #396 memory_sources named <project-dir>/<file>.md are resolved through memory_sources.py, a bad shape rejected as 'not a memory file name' and an unknown file as 'not a memory file on this host', and qualifying lists them as memory:<name>), file (threshold: 3 qualifying notes - insight, error-fix, decision, retro, session or migrated claude-memory; validation, reviewed-page refusal, refusal of an update that cites the page itself, every write path checked against the resolved wiki root (a symlinked queries/ is refused), scrub_secrets on question and body before the slug, projects taken from the sources (a payload projects field is ignored), name collisions get -2, -3...; shared vault OS ownership covers the page/index/log operation before the compatibility wiki lock; that compatibility lock refuses a living PID regardless of age; index.md rebuilt from the notes table and split into index-<project>.md files above 500 pages, log-YYYY.md; every write uses the shared transaction boundary; stale owned index files use revision-checked delete_note; an index or log failure after the page is written exits 0 with a warning key). memgrep (#396): reads {"pattern"} on stdin (non-blank, at most 200 characters), matches it as a case-insensitive fixed string against the files from memory_sources(detect_host()), prints {"host","matches":[{"name","path"}],"skipped":[{"path","error"}]} (skipped: listing failures, then files that could not be read). Memory files are fingerprinted under memory:<name>, and stale reports changed:/missing:/unverifiable: memory:<name>: unverifiable on a host other than claude-code, when the listing failed for the root, the project or the file, or when a listed file cannot be read; missing only when a listing that worked lacks the file. stale also returns memory_paths ({name: path} for cited memory files found here) so a refresh can re-read them; other callers ignore it. stale takes an optional memory_listing keyword (a _memory_listing() result) so a caller checking many pages lists memory files once. read_page splits a block-map line on the first ': ' (or a final ':'), so keys such as memory:proj/a.md survive, and a quoted key ends at its closing quote. render_wiki_index(ctx) returns {file name: text} from the notes table and writes nothing; rebuild_wiki_index writes it, and the wiki-pages doctor check compares against it. Pages live in <wiki_folder>/queries/YYYY/; index and log files carry type claude-wiki-index so the indexer skips them. Dates are the local date. Exit 0 ok, 1 refused (ERROR: line), 2 usage error or crash. Source revisions are recorded before index rendering. Stable filing IDs deduplicate page retries and log records. Reviewed pages remain protected; a corrupt log stays unchanged and produces a warning after valid page publication.

components.name: memory_sources.py
components.purpose: The one place that knows where a host keeps its memory files (#396). An explicit runtime context selects the host before inherited environment markers. Legacy detect_host() uses _CODEX_HOST_MARKERS, else claude-code. memory_sources(host, config=None, errors=None) returns sorted, resolved, unique paths: on claude-code or claude every regular, non-symlinked *.md directly inside a non-symlinked memory/ folder of a non-symlinked project folder under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects (default ~/.claude/projects), skipping MEMORY.md (an index) and checking resolved containment. Codex native memory discovery is explicitly unsupported: it returns [] and records an unsupported diagnostic in errors. failed_scopes treats that diagnostic as root_failed so wiki cleanup cannot prune unseen sources. config is retained for compatibility. memory_name(path) returns <project-dir>/<file>.md, the name pages and payloads use. An unreadable project is skipped, not fatal; when errors is a list, each failure (an unlistable root, an unreadable project or memory/ folder, an unresolvable file) is appended as {"path","error"}, and failed_scopes(errors) classifies them as (root_failed, projects, names) for wiki.stale. Skills never name these paths; they call wiki.py memgrep.

components.name: describe_plugin_install_divergence() / _read_plugin_version()
components.purpose: Version-skew probe (#318): enumerates every obsidian-brain install on disk (the marketplace directory-source checkout plus every ~/.claude/plugins/cache/*/obsidian-brain/*/) and warns when their manifest versions disagree, naming which one the caller's hooks actually resolved to. Replaces an original design gated on CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, verified NOT set in a skill's Bash block (Claude Code interpolates it into hooks.json command strings only, not skill shells) — a skill cannot introspect which copy of its own SKILL.md Claude Code loaded, so the probe compares installs against each other instead of 'this skill' against 'these hooks'. _read_plugin_version() checks <path>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, <path>/plugin.json, then the same two on the parent — the parent rungs are what let a hooks/ directory input resolve at all, since this repo's own manifest lives at .claude-plugin/plugin.json one level above hooks/. Both functions accept injected paths so callers (and tests) never touch the real plugin tree; skills/check-items/SKILL.md Step 1 calls it with no arguments and prints any warning to stderr, swallowing all exceptions — a diagnostic must never break the command it diagnoses.

components.name: note_transactions.py
components.purpose: Shared vault mutation boundary. Persistent OS ownership is acquired in vault then session order; living holders are never replaced by age. Records source revisions and managed capture/summary hashes, journals immutable operation payloads before atomic publication, then records applied revisions. Retries reuse operation IDs. Whole-document writes require an exact source revision; managed updates preserve edits outside their region and summaries also check capture provenance. Conflicts preserve the note and return conflict; lock contention or recoverable failures return pending work in private state. Modes preserve existing permissions unless the writer requests 0600 or 0644. Ordinary writes refuse invalid UTF-8. Explicit repair_document uses a recorded raw-byte revision. Journaled moves require an absent destination and never overwrite it; journaled deletes and rollback require the expected revision, preserving later replacements and edits.

components.name: capture.py
components.purpose: Retains scrubbed capture facts and an immutable checkpoint body before note publication. Event identity includes host/native session, source, generation and event ID; facts remain together when a session resumes in another worktree. Source ownership-marker text is escaped after scrubbing. Checkpoint ready phase freezes the selected expected revision before the note operation is prepared. A later checkpoint may advance its baseline only when an earlier recorded publication proves the current capture hash. Recovery never changes a ready operation payload or overwrites a manual capture edit. Applied publication precedes cursor acknowledgment. Historical pending rows without immutable bodies stay pending with a warning. source_sessions retains selected source descriptors, cursors, native state, completeness, first date, and message count; native_events retains scrubbed normalized facts before any message-threshold publication. The registered-source recovery queue rotates through a bounded batch without a full-vault scan. PreCompact writes immutable snapshots identified by native session, capture-region revision, and trigger, with a stable parent-session link. Native compact/clear trigger and snapshot toggles are explicit. Snapshots default to the legacy sessions folder and preserve their parent link. Conversation markdown cannot become note structure. Consecutive coordination messages render as a count without dropping private identity receipts. Snapshot creation timestamps persist by immutable operation identity.

components.name: Native transcript adapters
components.purpose: Shared bounded strict-JSONL reader verifies selected native identity and source containment, retains malformed or incomplete offsets, and detects source rotation/truncation with generations and anchors. SourceCursor carries bounded parser state; SourceRecord carries visible user/assistant messages, explicit tool names with unknown category, and fixed control records. Codex native message mirrors are deduplicated by ID or cross-kind occurrence proof, while distinct human repeats survive. Reasoning, encrypted content, environment, developer instructions, and HookPrompt are excluded. A full fork selects a matching child session_meta within the bounded batch and excludes proven parent-owned records. Ambiguous inherited facts and missing child metadata stay pending within the bounded search. Read-only native provenance verified the observed synthetic fork starts with its child session_meta at byte 0, ordinal 30; a larger inherited prefix is not an observed acceptance blocker. Shared reader qualifies byte-offset fallback identities by source generation. Well-formed unknown or ownership-ambiguous rows retain bounded private offset/hash references without raw bodies; verified later rows can publish while completeness stays partial. Replay rechecks source identity and exact bytes, rotates a bounded queue, and resolves understood metadata without inventing chat. Malformed or incomplete rows remain cursor-blocking. Native capture sorts late facts only within a verified source generation; uncertain cross-generation order gets a late-replay label. SessionStart and doctor expose safe type labels and pending lower bounds. Each JSONL row is bounded to 1 MiB and forward reads to 4 MiB per call. Oversized rows are drained without loading their bodies under the same deadline and retained as generic unresolved references; verified later rows may publish partial capture. Opaque verification/draining stops at 256 MiB or 256 chunks with 1 MiB buffers; beyond stays pending.

components.name: Native lifecycle dispatch
components.purpose: Shared bounded Start/resume, Stop, PreCompact and End handlers capture before legacy retro gates, retain pending input, and recover bounded registered sources. Claude and Codex descriptors enter native_entry. Each bound SessionEnd handler appends one private outcome log entry; bootstrap failures without a verified context report only to stderr. Fixtures prove shared behavior, not actual Desktop dispatch.

components.name: ai_backend.py + native adapters
components.purpose: Runs six analysis operations through the explicit invoking host only. Requests carry inline scrubbed input, source revision, bounded timeout and exact coverage options. Native subprocess input/output and deadlines are bounded; nested-job markers keep capture hooks from recording internal analysis. Strict JSON/schema and semantic checks reject malformed, missing, duplicate or foreign IDs. No provider fallback or model-written vault paths. AIResult.model is the observed actual model, or unknown; requested aliases are not execution evidence.

components.name: operation_state.py
components.purpose: Authored skill stages receive an explicit UUID operation ID and owner-only jobs directory keyed by vault, host, native session and canonical project. Private artifacts stay outside the vault, reject symlinks and use SHA-registered manifests. Fixed shared handlers validate inputs and publish vault edits through the transaction service. Source revisions are captured before AI; stale sources retain user bytes and pending work.

components.name: session_lookup.py
components.purpose: Read-only bounded lookup verifies full host/native session identity in frontmatter before adopting an existing session note. Short display hashes, a changed date or another project worktree do not prove identity. Candidate overflow, ambiguous matches, unusable index or deadline expiry stays pending. It does not scan the whole vault, create an index or guess a host.

components.name: Native hook entry and descriptors
components.purpose: Selects native actor and verified current client before dispatch. Codex events without client proof report skipped capture and no retained source on stderr; another frontend is never inferred from transcript origin.

components.name: Private session auxiliary state
components.purpose: Owner-only caches, calendar, locks and retro decisions use vault, host, native session ID and canonical project root. State remains outside the selected vault and rejects symlinks.

layers.name: Search & Index (SQLite + FTS5)
layers.description: A local SQLite database (WAL mode, FTS5) that enables fast full-text and ranked recall across the vault. Lazy mtime-incremental sync, a 7-signal reranker, ACT-R activation from an access log, and TF-IDF cosine themes with a Free-Energy surprise signal. Hooks never touch this — it is skill-side only.

components.name: ensure_index() / _sync()
components.purpose: Create-or-update the DB: schema init statement-by-statement (FTS5 IF NOT EXISTS), column migrations, mtime-incremental sync inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and corruption recovery that deletes+recreates db/-wal/-shm. When a single sync churns >50% of the final corpus — via inserts OR deletions combined — _recompute_all_tfidf_vectors() runs a second pass so TF-IDF scores reflect the final N/df: inserts otherwise leave early notes with insertion-time IDF, and deletions otherwise leave survivors with pre-deletion IDF (#235) until the next mtime-triggered upsert. Notes whose type is in _UNINDEXED_TYPES ({claude-wiki-index}: the LLM wiki's own index and log files, #383) are skipped and counted as 'excluded'; a row whose note changed to such a type is deleted.

components.name: search_vault()
components.purpose: Sanitizes the query to AND-mode FTS5 (hyphens to spaces), runs bm25 with title 10x and tags 5x weighting, OR-fallback when AND is empty, reranks, batch-logs access, strips body before returning. Two opt-in additions: include_vectors=True adds a decoded tfidf_vector key (dict[str,float] or None) to each result, used by /compress Step 3.5 for the cosine gate; every result dict also carries an or_fallback bool (True when retrieved via the OR-fallback branch).

components.name: compute_query_vector()
components.purpose: Computes a sparse TF-IDF vector for a search query against the live corpus (vault_index.py). Takes a db_path string (consistent with search_vault) and manages its own connection via _connect with try/finally close. Uses the same tokenization and IDF weighting as _upsert_note but without the caller-side total_docs pre-increment that _upsert_note applies for a new insert (effective N = COUNT(*)+1 for a query vs COUNT(*)+2 for a fresh insert — a one-document offset, negligible at any realistic corpus size). Returns {} for empty/stopword-only queries — callers treat {} as a signal to skip cosine gating. Used by /compress Step 3.5 to produce query_vec passed into is_high_confidence_match.

components.name: rerank_results() — 7-signal scorer
components.purpose: Weighted sum: proximity 0.25, bm25 0.20, activation 0.20, type 0.10, recency 0.10, importance 0.10, density 0.05. Type score has a column per context (debugging/standup/emerge/search/general). Only the general column is used in production today: search_vault picks another context only when a caller passes caller=, and no caller does. Every note type a writer emits has an explicit weight in every context (tests/test_type_scores.py scans hooks/, scripts/, skills/ and templates/ for them, #376); a missing type would fall back to 0.5. claude-stats and claude-check-items-report score 0.0, and claude-emerge scores 0.0 in the emerge context. 0.0 is a down-weight, not an exclusion: it lowers the final score by at most 0.05 against the 0.5 default. claude-wiki (#383) weighs the same as claude-insight in every context.

components.name: log_access() / batch_activations()
components.purpose: Records access events (cascading snapshot accesses to the parent session) and computes ACT-R base-level activation, reserving 0.0 for notes with no history.

components.name: tfidf.py — TF-IDF primitives (leaf)
components.purpose: Stdlib-only leaf (no vault_index or themes imports). Exports _tokenize_for_tfidf, _compute_tfidf_vector, _cosine_similarity, _update_term_df, _reverse_fold_centroid, _STOPWORDS, _TOKEN_RE. Smoothed IDF, sparse top-50 vectors, cosine similarity. _reverse_fold_centroid does the reverse-fold removal of a note's vector from a running-average centroid, shared by themes.assign_to_theme and vault_index._delete_note (#246). Imported by themes.py and re-exported from vault_index.py for back-compat; kept acyclic by design. term_df maintained via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, never blind REPLACE.

components.name: themes.py — theme lifecycle + query/activation layer
components.purpose: Full theme lifecycle: creation (create_theme), incremental assignment (assign_to_theme), merge (merge_themes), split support via _theme_member_vectors, Free-Energy surprise detection (detect_surprise), centroid math (compute_centroid), and read helpers (get_unassigned_notes, get_all_vectorized_notes, theme_stats). Adds the theme-query/activation layer for /emerge and /recall (#231): recompute_activation() writes themes.activation as the ACT-R recency-decayed sum over member added_date (0.5 ** age/HALF_LIFE_DAYS, half-life 30d); get_themes_in_window() / get_top_themes_for_project() rank by activation DESC; get_theme_member_previews() returns top-N members by similarity with truncated excerpts; get_unassigned_notes_in_window() lists vectorized, theme-less notes in a date window. Extracted from vault_index.py (#229). Depends on tfidf (one-directional); lazy-imports vault_index._connect at call-time to break the import cycle. assign_to_theme() prefilters theme candidates by term-overlap before computing cosine, and accepts optional note_text to compute surprise via detect_surprise within the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. merge_themes() guards against self-merge (a==b) before opening any DB connection. assign_to_theme() enforces single-theme membership (#234): on reassignment to a different best theme it vacates the note's prior theme_members row and reconciles that theme's note_count + centroid (reverse-fold, mirroring _delete_note), so a note belongs to at most one theme.

components.name: rebuild_index() — Friston-preserving
components.purpose: Default non-destructive rebuild preserves access_log, themes and theme_members (activation/centroid/surprise), with an absolute-path safety guard that skips orphan-prune on path-format drift. Also runs _backfill_missing_tfidf_vectors() to populate tfidf_vector for any notes that still have it NULL (notes indexed before the vector-storage migration), so the /compress cosine gate applies to all candidates rather than fail-opening on vectorless notes (#255). full=True is the legacy total wipe for corrupt schema. Preserve mode reports foreign_deleted: rows dropped for being outside every scanned folder (#383).

components.name: _upsert_note() — DELETE-then-INSERT
components.purpose: Deliberately avoids INSERT OR REPLACE: explicit DELETE+INSERT preserving the prior importance value, and issuing the contentless-FTS5 delete op with old column values so the FTS index never accumulates orphans. Token-scoped term_df fetch: only fetches df rows for terms in the current note (chunked IN clause at 900 placeholders), not a full-table scan, so cost is O(note tokens) not O(vocabulary).

components.name: compute_stats()
components.purpose: Read-only aggregation for /vault-stats: signal coverage (per-note activation + importance), access-by-context, top-accessed, importance distribution, and snapshot integrity metrics (orphans, broken backlinks, summarized fraction).

layers.name: Triage Pipeline (check-items / emerge / standup-deep)
layers.description: The Python support layer behind /check-items, /standup deep and /emerge. A staged pipeline — L1 cache to token grouping to semantic merge to evidence gather to L2 deterministic prefilter to chunked LLM classification to partition to dashboard — with tight false-positive guards and a heuristic fallback.

components.name: check_items_args.py
components.purpose: Order-independent Scope parsing: mode (current/vault/project), Nd window, --show-all/--dry-run/--no-cache, and project detection against known workspace dirs. parse_scope() now unions workspace-root projects with every vault-index project (degrading to empty on any lookup failure, never raising) and records any token matching neither as scope.unknown_tokens; SKILL.md Step 1 exits 2 on a non-empty set rather than silently falling back to the current-project scope, naming the token(s) and a substring+difflib 'Did you mean' suggestion (#318).

components.name: check_items_prefilter.py
components.purpose: L2 deterministic triage: classifies items with no plausible completion evidence without dispatching a sub-agent. Distinctiveness gate (snake_case / len>=8 / interior mixed-case) is the key false-positive guard against generic short words. synthetic_classification() emits a third no-evidence tier — REVIEW — for items under the 90-day STALE threshold whose canonical text carries a distinctive token (names a shipped-looking component/branch/feature) but has no anchor and no evidence overlap, so they surface for human judgment instead of silently landing ACTIVE (#264).

components.name: check_items_cache.py
components.purpose: Replay requires matching complete input/evidence, vault and canonical project, local classifier prompt/policy, actual shared backend output schema, analysis instruction, validation policy and known backend/model identity. Successful observed full model IDs are retained. Claude haiku/sonnet/opus/fable aliases cannot authorize replay, including a prior observed alias resolution; unknown native defaults miss. Explicit known full model settings permit matching replay. Cache writes require ownership and do not publish incomplete classifications.

components.name: check_items_cli.py
components.purpose: Inline semantic-merge and classifier requests use the invoking native backend. Classifier chunks must return every requested group ID exactly once; exhausted, cancelled or unavailable chunks publish no partial result. Validated results are atomically written as private JSON under the explicit session jobs namespace, never to a model-supplied path. Claude threshold aliases remain invocation policy; an explicit full classifier_model controls only Claude classification. Codex uses its native model/profile selection.

components.name: check_items_report.py
components.purpose: Writes the per-scope dashboard note (Done/Needs-Action/Review/Stale/Active sections + classifier-mode frontmatter), always written even on --dry-run, path-contained and atomic. The '## Review' section (#264) lists items neither the L2 prefilter nor the sub-agent classifier could confirm DONE but which name shipped-looking work, so they surface visibly instead of landing silently in Active. Since #320 F1, the frontmatter and prose summary also carry a 'skipped' count (default 0) next to 'cascaded', threaded from /check-items Step 8's cascade summary -- the count of sibling checkoff candidates that were refused (drift, unverifiable text, checkbox already gone) or lost to a failed write, so the dashboard cannot silently drop those candidates down to only the auto-checked count. Two further #318 additions: (1) write_check_items_dashboard() takes an optional evidence_gaps dict (from deep_analysis_pipeline's output, threaded via SKILL.md Step 5's gaps.json) and renders a '## Evidence Gaps' section plus an evidence_gaps frontmatter field ONLY when a real gap exists — omitting the argument is a true no-op for every existing caller; (2) 'merges' is now normalised before rendering ('## Merged Groups' previously crashed with TypeError when a caller passed a bare count instead of open_item_dedup.merge_records_from_groups()'s record list — a non-list value now renders an explicit 'Merged Groups unavailable' warning naming the bad input instead). A third change reworks checkbox rendering generally: every checkbox (Done/Needs-Action/Review) now renders '- [x]' from c.get('applied') — whether Step 8 actually flipped that record — not from its classification, and the Done heading counts only applied DONE items with a summary line naming flips applied outside DONE.

components.name: open_item_dedup.py
components.purpose: Cross-note open-item dedup (exact to distinctive-token to fuzzy set-intersection), cascade-checkoff with verify-before-edit, the heuristic fallback classifier (distinctive token AND completion phrase within +/-120 chars in the same sentence, minus the #299 conditional guard), the deep_analysis_pipeline evidence engine, and anchor_text_matches/_normalize_item_text — the text-anchor helper (#201) that confirms a checkbox line is the open item meant for checkoff via a normalized longest-common-substring threshold. cascade_group_members (/check-items sibling cascade) and batch_cascade_checkoff (/standup cascade) now also text-anchor their targets (#250): each carries the member's/duplicate's own stored text alongside its (file, line) key and, at flip time, flips a line ONLY when it still passes the pre-existing '- [ ] ' checkbox-prefix guard (unchanged — prevents prose corruption) AND anchor_text_matches(line, stored_text) (new — prevents flipping a DIFFERENT active item the line drifted onto). This is deliberately verify-don't-re-resolve, NOT a mirror of #201 Guard B's 'unique text match -> act, 2+ matches -> refuse': a cascade group or duplicate set IS a set of near-identical lines by construction, so refusing on 2+ matches would refuse exactly the case the cascade exists to serve and silently under-flip; verifying each target against its OWN stored index instead — never re-searching the file for a replacement line — closes the drift hole while still flipping every legitimate sibling. Blank/missing stored text is treated as unverifiable and skipped rather than flipped. Skips (drift, unverifiable-blank-text, or checkbox-already-gone -- #320 F4 moved the last of these out of stderr-only) are each reported to stderr AND appended to the returned summary string via the shared _format_text_verification_skips() helper, now parameterised on wording per skip class (capped at 5 enumerated file:line entries + a '+N more' tail), so a hook caller that never surfaces stderr still sees them and can tell the three classes apart. A verified flip whose atomic os.replace() write fails is no longer silently lost either (#320 F2): it is named in a trailing 'WRITE FAILED for N file(s); M verified flip(s) were NOT saved: ...' summary line, and once ANY target existed the summary never collapses back to the empty-input 'No member lines to cascade.' / 'No duplicates found for cascading.' wording -- a run where every candidate was refused or lost instead reads 'Cascaded 0 ... -- every candidate was refused or failed to save.' (#320 F3), reserving the empty-input wording for a genuinely empty run. The residual, undocumented-no-longer gap: a drifted line that is ITSELF text-similar enough to anchor (a genuine reword) still flips, since re-resolution cannot distinguish that from a coincidental sibling. deep_analysis_pipeline now also collects bounded/deduped recent git tags and default-branch changed paths as ground truth; fold_tags_and_paths_into_completion_zone() folds both into the completion-zone evidence bucket check_items_prefilter.has_classifiable_evidence() reads (#264 Task 2). partition_for_review() (Stage 5) routes DONE/NEEDS-ACTION/REVIEW into the visible 'review' bucket (REVIEW keeps its evidence_citation, unlike scrubbed ACTIVE) and ACTIVE (+STALE by default) into dashboard_only; assign_tier() caps REVIEW confidence at MED since a REVIEW verdict is definitionally uncertain (#264 Task 1). classify_groups_with_agent() (#297 defect 1) forwards the child classifier CLI's captured stderr to the parent on every failed attempt and prints a terminal diagnostic, so a classifier failure is never silent; get_last_classifier_mode() is three-valued — 'ok' (every group classified), 'partial' (some group_ids missing from a chunked run, #297 defect 2), or 'heuristic-fallback' (both attempts failed for every chunk). Every verdict now carries a classifier_source ('agent' | 'prefilter' | 'heuristic' | 'cache'); assign_tier() takes a 4th classifier_source param and fails CLOSED via module-level _HIGH_TRUST_SOURCES = frozenset({'agent','prefilter','cache'}) — an unknown or absent source caps the tier at MED, so a heuristic verdict can never be auto-checked (#297 defect 3, replacing an earlier denylist form that failed open). classify_groups_heuristic() likewise caps its own DONE verdicts' confidence at MED — its token-co-occurrence evidence can never justify HIGH at any proximity distance. classify_groups_heuristic() also applies the #299 conditional/forward-looking guard before emitting DONE, over ALL (token, phrase) pairs in a member text (capped at _HEURISTIC_MAX_MATCHES=20 of each, so a pair past the cap can only lose a DONE, never invent one) rather than the first of each: a pair must sit in one sentence, and the co-occurrence is rejected when a pending-intent cue (waiting on / blocked / pending / depends on / confirm / verify / validate / check / track / monitor, plus re-/cross-/double-/self- prefixed forms, searched across the enclosing sentence) governs it, or when a time/condition subordinator (once / until / if / when / after / whether, clipped to the enclosing clause) is paired with a forward-looking verb form (is|are|be|get(s)|modal, within _FORWARD_FORM_LOOKBACK_CHARS=24 chars before the phrase AND inside that same clause — BOTH halves of the tier-2 test share the clause scope, since clipping only the cue left its corroboration search floored at the SENTENCE start, so a modal in a PRECEDING clause could corroborate a cue in this one and reject a bare-past claim ('It will ship; once #51 merged.' cited the 'will' from the clause next door — reported rather than silent, but crediting corroboration the documented scope excludes; inert on live data, 0 verdict and 0 citation changes across all three corpora). Past forms (was/were/has been) are excluded so bare-past completion claims survive. All four regexes are anchored to prose, not to \b: _COMPLETION_PHRASE_RE adds a trailing (?!-(?!particle)) so 'release' inside the compound post-release-verification is not a completion claim (a live vault item that flipped ACTIVE→DONE without it; all 10 live member texts carrying a <completion-word>-<word> shape are compounds of that kind, so the anchor cannot simply be dropped), while a LEADING hyphen still reads as one (auto-merged / back-merged) and a trailing verb PARTICLE that forms the WHOLE final hyphen-segment (_COMPLETION_PARTICLES = in / into / out / up / off / over / back / through / down; 'on' deliberately excluded to keep 'merged-on main' / 'closed-on friday' — branch/date qualifiers, not phrasal verbs — blocked, NOT to block the live 'Development-Complete-on-board', which the whole-segment rule blocks either way since its 'on' is followed by '-board') is let through — a bare (?![-\w]) rejected 'merged-in with #51' and 'closed-out last week' SILENTLY, since no other pair in those texts qualifies and the guard had no rejection to cite; the cue and forward-form regexes are anchored with (?<![\w./-]) / (?![\w./-]) so check-pr-base.py, scripts/verify.sh and `go.get.it` cannot supply a cue from an identifier fragment — with one deliberate exception: _CONDITIONAL_CUE_RE OMITS the slash, (?<![\w.-]) / (?![\w.-]), because a slash joins prose alternatives as readily as path segments and with it in the class 'Bump the cache if/when #51 is merged' matched NEITHER cue ('if' failed the trailing anchor, 'when' the leading one), silencing tier 2 on the most explicitly conditional phrasing there is (if/when appears in the live corpus). That is safe for tier 2 alone, which additionally requires forward-form corroboration a bare path segment cannot give; tier 1 rejects on its cue alone and therefore keeps the slash — a known, deliberate limit is that a slash-joined TIER-1 pair ('confirm/verify') still fires neither cue (0 such pairs in the live corpus). The DOT, kept in every class, is what actually protects the `go.get.it` case. Sentence/clause boundaries split on a BLANK line, not a bare newline (a wrapped line is one sentence), and not on an abbreviation drawn from the literal ALLOWLIST _ABBREV_LOOKBEHINDS (e.g. / i.e. / etc. / vs., one fixed-width lookbehind per spelling since Python lookbehinds cannot alternate widths); anything outside that list — an initial such as A.B., or Dr. — intentionally DOES end the sentence, because the letter-dot-letter SHAPE this replaced also matched INITIALS and merged two sentences into one, letting a tier-1 cue in the first half govern a genuine completion in the second (allowlist not denylist, as with _HIGH_TRUST_SOURCES). _segment_start() scans the full text and stops at the first boundary ending past pos rather than passing pos as finditer's endpos, which made $ match there and invent a boundary. A rejected verdict stays ACTIVE but carries a 'heuristic: DONE rejected — ...' evidence_citation naming the token, phrase and cue, and is logged to stderr, because partition_for_review() scrubs evidence_citation on ACTIVE. The two guard log kinds are greppable apart and each quotes the group's canonical text (whitespace-collapsed to one line, 80 chars) rather than only an opaque group_id: 'heuristic-guard DONE-REJECTED:' for a verdict the guard refused, 'heuristic-guard DONE-DISPUTED:' for a DONE carrying a sibling member's objection — so grep 'DONE rejected' still selects only the former. A pair the same-sentence gate drops is reported the same way (lower precedence than a real cue rejection) instead of vanishing with evidence_citation None, and that precedence — cue over boundary over compound-phrase — holds ACROSS members as well as within one: the earlier first-come choice ignored the rejection KIND, so one group with the same two members reported the uninformative boundary reason or the governing cue purely by member ORDER. A cue or boundary rejection recorded against one member survives a SIBLING member's DONE — appended to the DONE citation as '(sibling member rejected at <file>:<line>: ...)' and logged with the same location — because SKILL.md Step 8 cascades a DONE group's checkoff to every member (file, line) it has, including the line the guard judged not done, so the objection has to name THAT line and not merely the group representative the log already quotes (_member_location() omits the suffix when a member carries no usable file/line rather than printing 'None'). A COMPOUND rejection is deliberately excluded from that sibling path: it is reached only when the member had no in-range (token, surviving-phrase) pair at all — the same evidentiary state as a member carrying no completion language whatsoever, which raises no objection — so DONE-DISPUTED on it split two indistinguishable absences and diluted the signal on genuinely contested lines. A boundary rejection is reachable only from inside the proximity check, so it always names a real token and a surviving phrase the guard declined to credit, and stays. The compound reason still rides on the ACTIVE citation, where it explains a real downgrade. _COMPLETION_PHRASE_RE and _DISTINCTIVE_TOKEN_RE gate that pair loop from upstream, so a narrowing of either one that suppresses a text's ONLY completion phrase or ONLY token used to build no pair at all: _heuristic_member_verdict returned (None, None, None), the cue and boundary machinery never ran, and the record was an ACTIVE with evidence_citation None and nothing on stderr — silent by construction, and indistinguishable from a text with no completion language in it. That is how the trailing compound anchor swallowed 'This was merged-in with #51', and a replay over 3671 live open-item texts (every vault '- [ ]' line plus every merged.json member text) still found 2 downgrades reaching production through that channel. The PHRASE side is now CLOSED: when no pair survives the loop, _compound_phrase_rejection() re-scans with _LOOSE_COMPLETION_PHRASE_RE — the pre-#299 shape, generated from the same _COMPLETION_WORDS list without the compound anchor, so a match it finds and _COMPLETION_PHRASE_RE does not is by construction a completion word inside a hyphenated compound — and reports the pair as a _COMPOUND_PHRASE_REASON rejection, ranked BELOW cue and boundary because it explains an ABSENCE of evidence rather than naming a reason the item is open. Its reason text states the condition that actually routes a text there — no phrase that SURVIVED the gate sat within range of a token — not 'no phrase survived the gate', which is false whenever a surviving phrase merely sits out of range (2 of the 4 compound citations on the live 3671-text corpus are of that shape). Reporting-only: verdicts are unchanged on all three corpora (398 merged.json groups 22->16 DONE / 6 downgrades; 1039 claude-sessions lines 24->15 / 9; 3671 wide 63->42 / 21; 0 upgrades and 0 silent downgrades everywhere). The TOKEN side is NOT closed — _DISTINCTIVE_TOKEN_RE has no loose counterpart — so any future narrowing of IT must still be justified against a live-corpus replay (which live texts lose their ONLY match), not against a synthetic fixture. Both reason constants are compared by VALUE at the bucketing sites, never by identity: an equal-but-reconstructed string would otherwise fall into the cue bucket and invert the precedence with nothing failing. #318: deep_analysis_pipeline no longer silently `continue`s past a project with no resolved local git repo (previously capping every item in it at tier LOW with DONE structurally unreachable, with no signal that anything was wrong). gather_note_completion_evidence() is now the evidence source for such a project: it mirrors /recall's contradicted_by signal, flagging an item when a STRICTLY NEWER session's own '## Summary' reports it done, gated on the same completion-phrase guard the heuristic classifier uses so a bare co-mention can never fabricate DONE evidence. The pipeline's output JSON gains an evidence_gaps block (projects_scanned, projects_with_evidence, projects_without_repo, all_projects_gapped) and a stderr warning naming the gap; SKILL.md Step 5 persists it to a sibling gaps.json (never folded into evidence.json, whose project-keyed shape check_items_cli._bridge_project_evidence() reads by treating every top-level key as a project name, which has no room for a gap-count/list-shaped metadata block). merge_records_from_groups() adapts merge_groups_semantically()'s surviving-group shape (each carrying absorbed_reasoning) into the canonical_group_id/absorbed_group_ids/reasoning records check_items_report._body actually reads for '## Merged Groups' — the shape merge_groups_semantically itself never produced, which is why a caller had nothing correct to pass and resorted to a bare count. Vault edits record the exact source revision and publish through NoteMutation/apply_mutations; conflict or pending results never count as applied edits.

components.name: compress_guard.py
components.purpose: is_high_confidence_match() predicate for /compress dedup: absolute-strength gate (top rank <= MIN_RANK_STRENGTH -5.0) AND rank-delta gate (top minus runner-up > MIN_RANK_DELTA 0.25), PLUS an optional OR-fallback-aware TF-IDF cosine gate. Cosine-rescue (#254): when the rank-delta gate fails but the top result has a stored tfidf_vector with cosine >= MIN_COSINE_RESCUE (0.40), the delta verdict is flipped True and evaluation continues into the cosine gate — a strong semantic match rescues a borderline BM25 near-miss. When caller supplies query_vec: if the top result has a stored tfidf_vector, cosine(query_vec, note_vec) >= MIN_COSINE (default 0.12) is required for both AND and OR-fallback hits. If no vector is stored: OR-fallback hits (or_fallback=True) are rejected fail-CLOSED (cannot confirm semantic closeness for a generic-token match — the #252/#108 false-positive class); AND-path hits (or_fallback absent/False) remain fail-OPEN (all query terms matched, rank confidence sufficient). Cosine gate entirely skipped when query_vec is None (backward compat). Constants MIN_RANK_STRENGTH/MIN_RANK_DELTA/MIN_COSINE/MIN_COSINE_RESCUE/MIN_TERM_OVERLAP are module-level and overridable per-call for tuning. Also exposes two pure evidence helpers for the Step 3.5 adjudication prompt (#189): summarize_match_evidence() returns the top rank, runner-up rank, a calibration band (very strong/strong/moderate/borderline by |rank|), and the query∩note shared TF-IDF terms; topic_snippet() extracts the matched note's first substantive paragraph.

components.name: deep_cli.py
components.purpose: Thin CLI backing /standup deep: runs the deep pipeline, renders the presentation, and applies path-contained batch edits with a 24h acted-on store so items are not re-recommended. The /standup deep checkoff path is text-anchored (#201): run_build_checkoffs re-resolves each target by text against the file's real unchecked-checkbox lines (ignoring drifted classifier line hints), refuses ambiguous matches (>1 distinct unchecked checkbox text-matching the representative) instead of guessing — the classifier line is a diagnostic hint only, never used to select a target, and emits verified triples; run_batch_edit line-anchors every checkbox flip (exact full-line match), surfaces any flip with no matching line as a skipped-checkoff list, and keeps the substring path only for non-checkbox edits like link additions. (The /check-items sibling-cascade path — cascade_group_members / batch_cascade_checkoff in open_item_dedup.py — is now also text-anchored, via verify-don't-re-resolve rather than Guard B's re-resolution; #250.) All four stdin entry points (run_pipeline, run_present, run_batch_edit, run_build_checkoffs) now read through one _read_stdin_capped() helper (1M-character cap, reject-not-truncate) — two of them previously called json.load(sys.stdin) directly, an unbounded read the stdin-cap AST guard could not see because it only recognized a `.read` attribute call (#275). Vault edits record the exact source revision and publish through NoteMutation/apply_mutations; conflict or pending results never count as applied edits.

components.name: emerge_cli.py
components.purpose: Thin CLI backing /emerge (theme-level). run_emerge_themes(days) refreshes theme activation (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), pulls themes updated in the window with their top-3 member previews plus windowed unassigned candidates, and writes a compact emerge-themes.json corpus atomically; emits STATUS=SPARSE:<n> (and writes nothing) when fewer than 2 themes are in the window. run_build_note() assembles the claude-emerge note from the sub-agent's emerge-analysis.md. The raw-note corpus path (run_corpus/run_recollect) was retired.

components.name: consolidate_cli.py
components.purpose: Thin CLI backing /consolidate: gathers unassigned (or all, with --full) note vectors, clusters per-project, names through the invoking native AI backend, persists themes + theme_members; stats/split/merge.

components.name: clustering.py
components.purpose: Pure single-linkage clustering over sparse TF-IDF vectors (connected components of the cosine>=threshold graph); numpy/scipy fast path, stdlib union-find fallback.

components.name: summarizer_metrics.py
components.purpose: Append-only JSONL telemetry for upgrade_batch() runs; rotates at 100 KB; never raises (best-effort stderr warn only).

layers.name: Vault Doctor (pluggable repair engine)
layers.description: A dispatcher plus an auto-discovered registry of repair checks. Each check implements scan() to list[Issue] and apply() to list[Result]. Dry-run by default; per-check crash containment; a --min-confidence filter that is override-safe because apply() raises on any non-canonical signal_class. Exit-code 2 escalates even at 0 issues when a check crashes.

components.name: vault_doctor.py
components.purpose: CLI dispatcher: config resolution (CLI > env > file, bypassing the session cache), flag forwarding via EXTRA_SCAN_FLAGS, per-check scan/apply crash containment with crashed_checks, the confidence filter with dropped_per_signal_class attribution, timestamped backup root, and the 0/1/2/3 exit-code contract. The interactive y/N low-confidence-issue confirm prompt now reads with sys.stdin.readline(1024) instead of an unbounded readline() — behaviourally identical for any real answer, but no longer able to consume to EOF on input with no newline (#275).

components.name: vault_doctor_checks/__init__.py
components.purpose: Auto-discovers checks via pkgutil; defines the Issue/Result dataclasses and the scan/apply module contract; all_checks() excludes OPT_IN=True checks; broken modules are warned-and-skipped, never fatal.

components.name: source-sessions
components.purpose: UUID-first stale source_session backlink detector across insights/decisions/error-fixes/retros. Skips imported notes; preserves mtime on repair so fixed notes do not re-enter the window; apply() raises on non uuid-basename-stale signal_class (conf 0.99).

components.name: crossed-source-session
components.purpose: Detects a note whose source_session contradicts the session_id of the note its own source_session_note wikilink resolves to - i.e. mis-attributed work, the observable damage in #330 (a retro stamping 18785285-... while linking a note whose session_id is 504f461a-...). Detection only: apply() always returns skipped and never writes, because deciding WHICH of the two ids is correct needs evidence the check does not have and a wrong repair would rewrite genuine attribution; the skipped Result says so, so --apply explains itself. confidence 0.95, so --min-confidence up to 0.9 does not silently drop it. Reports crossed pairs ONLY, never dangling links: a dangling backlink is the NORMAL mid-session state, since PreCompact writes a snapshot's forward reference before SessionEnd creates the parent - observed live while this shipped, where a peer session's healthy retro (source_session hashing to 83f5, backlink naming 83f5) pointed at a note that did not exist yet. The live vault holds 40 such links against one genuine crossing, so reporting them would bury the signal; snapshot-integrity and #214 own that space. Reads notes through a pure, uncached frontmatter parser (_parse_note_metadata_uncached), NOT obsidian_utils.read_note_metadata() - that helper's session cache does a cache_get/cache_set round-trip against ~/.claude/obsidian-brain/cache-<sid>.json on every call, and with this check's own unbounded scan (DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS=9999) that both balloons the cache file (measured 1.32MB on a 2472-note vault) and pins pre-edit field values for the life of the process, so a re-scan after a human hand-fixes a crossed note's source_session would still report it unresolved - the one check whose entire workflow is a human fixing that field by hand. Both folder-existence is_dir() checks are wrapped against PermissionError (Python 3.13 raises it, rather than returning False, when a parent directory is mode 0o000), since one sits inside the loop over both scanned folders and an unguarded raise on the first would abort the scan before the second, readable folder is ever reached.

components.name: session-coverage (opt-in)
components.purpose: Detects JSONL transcripts with no session note (SessionEnd missed), replicating hook thresholds + snapshot-anchor bypass. --reconstruct shells out to replay-sessionend.py to write the note (conf 0.9); replay-JSON shape-guarded.

components.name: snapshot-integrity
components.purpose: Five sub-checks: orphan snapshots, broken backlinks, stale/missing session snapshot-lists, and summary-status mismatch. Project-blind sid-collision detection routes colliding sids to unresolved before any parent-based fix.

components.name: snapshot-migration
components.purpose: Ordered legacy-format migrations (filename HHMMSS, missing status/backlink, session snapshot-list). Tracks renamed paths/stems, re-checks collisions before os.rename, and rolls back a rename only if zero vault-wide wikilink rewrites succeeded.

components.name: project-name-canonicalization (opt-in)
components.purpose: Backfills the canonical main-repo project name vs worktree slug via git rev-parse, with a GIT_DIR env scrub so ambient vars cannot certify one bogus name vault-wide; strict UTF-8 decode in apply (defers to encoding-corruption).

components.name: project-name-normalization
components.purpose: Detects underscores in project frontmatter (personal_ws to personal-ws) and the matching project tag; frontmatter-only regex; conf 1.0.

components.name: spurious-wikilinks
components.purpose: Escapes unescaped double-brackets in conversation/tool-usage lines (bash test brackets parsed by Obsidian as phantom wikilinks); session folder only; conf 1.0.

components.name: encoding-corruption
components.purpose: Detects invalid UTF-8 bytes (grep Binary file matches); re-encodes with errors=replace; backs up raw original bytes before the atomic rewrite.

components.name: audit-historic-repairs (opt-in)
components.purpose: One-shot audit of prior doctor backups: classifies each note A (restore mtime-drift corruption) / B (keep) / C (ambiguous) / D (both-wrong); only category A auto-applies, restoring the oldest backup backlink. Loud no-op if the backup root is missing.

components.name: missing-frontmatter-fence
components.purpose: Repairs notes whose frontmatter lost its opening `---` (the leading-fence-eaten failure mode #269 stops going forward), which makes type/date/project/tags invisible to Dataview and every frontmatter-filtering tool. Fires only when all five hold: first line isn't already `---`, first line is key:-shaped, a closing `---` exists within the line bound, every line above that closing fence is frontmatter-shaped, AND that closing fence is at or past _MIN_FRONTMATTER_LINES (3) — below that floor a `Text` line followed by `---` is far more likely a valid CommonMark setext H2 heading than lost frontmatter, and 'repairing' one would silently turn a heading into a frontmatter block. All 9 genuinely damaged notes in the live vault carry 9-18 frontmatter lines, so the floor costs zero detection (#276 follow-up). Repair inserts `---` as a new first line only; atomic temp+rename with per-note backup and re-verification against the live file (#276).

components.name: memory-index (opt-in)
components.purpose: Detects drift between ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/*.md and that store's MEMORY.md — the only entry point loaded into context each session, so an entry missing its pointer line is silently unrecallable forever (#308). Reports orphans (transitive BFS from MEMORY.md; orphan-isolated when nothing links the entry at all, orphan-unreachable when only another orphan does), dangling index pointers, case-only pointer mismatches (index-case-mismatch: resolves on a case-insensitive filesystem, breaks on a case-sensitive one), stores with entries but no MEMORY.md, an index that names no file at all over a store that has entries (index-names-nothing: a summary row alongside the per-entry orphan rows, not instead of them), unreadable and undecodable entries, unreadable stores, and MEMORY.md size against the ~17 KB compaction threshold / ~24 KB read budget. Link matching is deliberately asymmetric: reachability counts markdown links, [[wikilinks]] and bare name.md mentions (under-counting invents orphans — markdown-links-only over-reported 98 vs 92, measured 2026-08-12), while dangling counts markdown links ONLY and only ones naming a direct child of the store — every CommonMark form that names one (](name.md), ](./name.md), ](name.md 'Title'), ](<name.md>)) — because MEMORY.md legitimately wikilinks Obsidian vault notes, prose cites CLAUDE.md, and a reference memory line may link a URL ending in .md. The index is decoded strictly: bad bytes there would silently report the whole store as orphaned. Entries are decoded leniently with an entry-undecodable row, and any entry that could not be read in full downgrades that store's orphan-isolated rows to orphan-unreachable. Report-only: every issue is unresolved/confidence 0.0, so --apply never writes to a memory store (and --min-confidence > 0 hides every row). One unreadable store is dropped from the report and gets a store-unreadable row; scan() raises only when every selected store fails, which the dispatcher turns into exit 2. A --project value matching no store at all emits a project-filter-matched-nothing row carrying stores_scanned/stores_filtered_out, so a filter typo cannot pass as a clean machine. Case folding applies to all three link kinds when deciding reachability (index-case-mismatch stays a markdown-link-only warning). vault_doctor.py's _issue_row surfaces this check's extras (entry_count, indexed_count, index_size_bytes, soft_limit_bytes, hard_limit_bytes, index_path, entry_names, byte_offset, read_error) conditionally, so --json consumers get the numbers without re-parsing reason and no other check's row shape moved. OPT_IN: a full run produced 92 rows across 7 projects (measured 2026-08-12), which would drown the default sweep.

components.name: wiki-pages
